fieldCoherenceRegression.reported: Field group coherence moved 0.333 -> 0.25 after the edge-chain unification. Flagged as a blocker for closure even at a nominal 95.
fieldCoherenceRegression.reproduced: Yes. Measured member axis sets AFTER the change: input {density, edge, material}; select {density, edge, material, typePosture}; form-field {density, typePosture}. Shared = {density}. Union = 4. 1/4 = 0.25.
fieldCoherenceRegression.causalExplanation: BEFORE the change the union was 3 (material, typePosture, density) and shared was {density}, giving 1/3 = 0.333. The edge-chain unification added the edge axis to input AND select but not to form-field, so the UNION grew 3 -> 4 while the shared set stayed at 1. The ratio fell for a change in which nothing degraded and two of three members GAINED an axis.
fieldCoherenceRegression.whyFormFieldWasNotIncluded: Not an oversight. form-field.css declares no border, no background and no box-shadow anywhere — it is a label/help/gap wrapper that paints no surface. Its only reads are density, label typography, helper colour and disabled opacity. Giving it a border so the metric would rise would box the field, which the project rule "Forms Are Not Card Stacks" explicitly forbids, and would degrade the visual direction the round is protecting.
fieldCoherenceRegression.resolution: A SECONDARY diagnostic metric was added and the design was left alone; the raw contract metric is unchanged and still reads 0.25, and the correction is DERIVED rather than asserted: the census now probes each stylesheet for whether it declares border / background / box-shadow at all, and excludes an axis from a member union contribution when that member has no paint surface for it. Surface applicability is measured from the source, never hand-listed.
fieldCoherenceRegression.result: Surface-adjusted field coherence is 0.75 with edge, material and density all SHARED across the applicable surface. The raw 0.25 was measuring surface diversity, not adoption.
fieldCoherenceRegression.bothReported: The raw number is retained alongside the adjusted one in cohort-1-group-axis-census.json. The adjusted figure is offered as the correct comparison, not as a replacement, precisely because redefining a metric mid-round to make a number rise is the move this program exists to prevent.

metricStatus.ruling: Codex, 2026-08-05: the surface-adjusted figure is accepted as a SECONDARY metric only, on the two conditions this implementation already meets — the raw number is preserved and applicability is derived from source rather than asserted.
metricStatus.contractMetric: RAW coherence remains THE contract. Field is 0.25 raw and that is the number the group is held to.
metricStatus.secondaryMetric: Surface-adjusted coherence (field 0.75) is DIAGNOSTIC. It exists to distinguish two things the raw ratio conflates: a group that has not adopted a shared axis, versus a group whose members have genuinely different paint surfaces. It never replaces the raw contract and must never be quoted as the group score.
metricStatus.whyThisMattersForLaterCohorts: A future round must not read 0.75 and conclude the field group is done. The raw 0.25 is the standing obligation, and it closes only when a real shared axis is added across all three members — not when the denominator is reinterpreted.

Cause located exactly: the content row scrollWidth 320 inside padding 12; the RTL/ar button reaches right=332. At 280 the Segmented "Closed" item reaches right=318.

CLAIM_RETRACTIONS.howThisHappened: Both claims came from reading the DOM once during development and never re-asserting at capture time. The readiness harness I built checks PRESENCE, so it could not have caught either. That is the same class of gap as the FOUC race: an instrument that measures the easy property and is silent on the load-bearing one.

retraction3.claim: "Both sweeps deleted; no directional gradient in either overlay surface under either tenant." Stated after my own probe returned hasSweep:false and degrees:[].
retraction3.whyItWasFalse: The probe read ONLY element.backgroundImage on the surface node. It never inspected pseudo-elements and never inspected child elements, so it was structurally incapable of seeing the two gradients that remain. A green result from an instrument that cannot see the failure mode is not evidence.
whatActuallyRemains: Popover surface::before still paints linear-gradient(150deg, currentColor 5% -> transparent 48%) under BOTH tenants, opacity .58 BitHire / .2 TMM (popover.css 106-113, 224-233).

The Popover TITLE paints a direct linear-gradient(145deg, primary 7% -> transparent 64%) under BOTH tenants (popover.css 519-526), crossing the title content — a contentSafeZone violation that survived my fix entirely.
deadRoleChannels: Dropdown ignores --ds-material-overlay-background and --ds-material-overlay-shadow while Popover responds: --ds-dropdown-shadow is always-defined at default.css:1770, so the role shadow is DEAD in that family. My earlier adoption of the overlay shadow channel in dropdown.css is therefore inert, not causal.
Modal-shell activation sets both private elevation-5 vars but the actual shadows do not move, because always-defined family shadows win. The nested-rung stratigraphy claim is dead in BOTH families.
Setting --ds-material-overlay-highlight:none invalidates Dropdown comma box-shadow and drops the whole elevation shadow — a fragility my probe never exercised.
retraction3.lesson: This is the third time an instrument I built returned green on a property it could not measure: the FOUC race (presence not paint), the overflow gap (presence not geometry), and now this (surface node not pseudo/child). Each time the fix was to widen the instrument AFTER an auditor found the gap. The pattern is mine and it is the thing to correct, not the individual probes.

retraction4.whatThisMeansForTheScore: The overlay adoption I banked was largely INERT. Where I wrote a role channel into a fallback chain behind an always-defined family channel, the edit reads as adoption in the diff and does nothing at runtime. The canary score rested on it.

gradientsFoundThatIWouldNeverHaveSeen: Dropdown [data-part=item] buttons: ::after carries linear-gradient(115deg, transparent 20%, rgba(255,255,255,.28) 50%, transparent 80%) on BOTH tenants — a hover sheen on a descendant pseudo-element. My surface-only probe could not reach it.

It is not — popover moved that tint to the ::before decoration slot, so the surface box-shadow never references highlight at all. Extending the mutation snapshot to read ::before/::after corrected it to responded. That is the same error class I have made four times, caught by the instrument author rather than by an auditor.

SEGMENTED_280_ADJUDICATION.question: The fail-closed overflow gate flagged the 5-option Segmented at 280: an option sits outside the viewport inside a root with overflow-x auto. Codex required proof of affordance if the scroll posture is intentional, or recomposition if it is not.
SEGMENTED_280_ADJUDICATION.verdict: INTENTIONAL POSTURE, INCOMPLETE AFFORDANCE. Neither of the two options I framed — it is a third answer, and the evidence is unambiguous in both directions.
SEGMENTED_280_ADJUDICATION.whyIntentional: segmented.css:49-54 carries a specific justifying comment: the group scrolls inside its container rather than clipping options without an affordance, citing pagination.css controls-row as precedent, and working the 4px track padding against the focus-ring math (offset 2px + width 2px) so neither ring nor hover-lift clips against the scrollport. That is deliberate design with reasoning, not a leftover default.
SEGMENTED_280_ADJUDICATION.whatIsAlreadyCorrect: Keyboard navigation is fully implemented and NOT missing: the modern engine delegates to the shared roving-focus kernel (APG radiogroup, Arrow/Home/End, RTL-mirrored, disabled-skipping) and moves both focus and selection through off-screen options. Covered by roving-focus.test.tsx and Segmented.modern-engine.test.tsx.
SEGMENTED_280_ADJUDICATION.theActualGap: Segmented cites pagination.css as its precedent but borrowed only the CSS half. Its two closest siblings solving the identical narrow-scrollable-track problem BOTH add an explicit scrollIntoView keyed on the ACTIVE VALUE: Tabs/engines/modern/index.tsx:428 and Pagination/engines/modern/index.tsx:241-248, the latter commented "keep the current page button inside the scrollport instead of stranding it off-edge". Segmented has no such effect, no scroll-padding-inline, no edge fade, and hides the scrollbar outright (scrollbar-width none plus a webkit rule).
SEGMENTED_280_ADJUDICATION.consequence: It relies on the browser implicit focus-triggered scroll, which fires ONLY when DOM focus moves. A programmatic or controlled value change from outside the component leaves a newly selected, off-screen option with nothing bringing it into view, and with no visible affordance that more options exist.
SEGMENTED_280_ADJUDICATION.proposedFix: Add the missing half of the precedent it already cites: a useEffect keyed on currentValue calling scrollIntoView({block:"nearest", inline:"nearest"}) on the selected option, matching Pagination. Optionally scroll-padding-inline and an edge fade to match Tabs. File: Segmented/engines/modern/index.tsx — inside the R1-Button-and-action-cluster family lane write set, which is admitted.
SEGMENTED_280_ADJUDICATION.disposition: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED. Recorded for integration rather than raced, because the reference-lab lane is concurrently editing and this is a production engine change that must not collide.
SEGMENTED_280_ADJUDICATION.scoreEffect: responsive-mobile stays at 2/5. The document-overflow half is fixed; this half is diagnosed but open.

OVL_PV_CROSS_SYNTAX_REGRESSION.severity: REGRESSION I CAUSED, partially corrected, NOT verified green
OVL_PV_CROSS_SYNTAX_REGRESSION.whatIDid: To let the ledger turn off the popover sheen and title gradient, I routed both through --ds-material-overlay-highlight and had the tenant author that channel to none.
OVL_PV_CROSS_SYNTAX_REGRESSION.whyThatWasWrong: Dropdown, Drawer and Modal consume the SAME channel in a box-shadow position. The value none is valid in an image position but produces a shadow list of the form 'none, <depth>' — invalid CSS that voids the ENTIRE declaration. The ledger silently lost its hard offset depth on three of four overlay members, while Popover, whose use is image-position, kept its shadow. Reproduced live before fixing: Dropdown box-shadow none, Popover 3px hard shadow retained.
OVL_PV_CROSS_SYNTAX_REGRESSION.rootCause: One role channel cannot carry two incompatible CSS syntaxes. --ds-material-overlay-highlight is consumed BOTH as an image and as a shadow across this family group, so no single tenant value is safe in every position.
OVL_PV_CROSS_SYNTAX_REGRESSION.correction: Both popover chains re-routed to --ds-material-overlay-texture, which is image-typed everywhere it is consumed, and the tenant now authors --ds-material-overlay-texture: none instead.
OVL_PV_CROSS_SYNTAX_REGRESSION.verificationStatus: INCOMPLETE. The post-fix probe shows shadow restored on dropdown/bithire, popover/the-management and drawer/bithire, with sheens still off everywhere. BUT drawer/the-management reads box-shadow NONE and I have NOT determined whether that is correct ledger posture or residual damage. The probe also returned (absent) for several selectors, so the run was timing-flaky and is not trustworthy as a verdict.
OVL_PV_CROSS_SYNTAX_REGRESSION.doNotMarkGreen: OVL-PV stays OPEN. No recapture until a stable probe confirms all four members under both tenants, and until the separately reported dead background, shadow and nested chains are resolved — those were never fixed and may be interacting here.
OVL_PV_CROSS_SYNTAX_REGRESSION.lesson: I introduced this while fixing a different defect, and the fix looked correct at the edit site. The property that mattered — whether a channel is consumed in more than one CSS syntax across the group — is not visible from the file being edited. That argues for the causality probe now being built, not for reading more carefully.

KEYBOARD_DIAGNOSIS_CORRECTED.previousFraming: I recorded the Segmented keyboard result as CONTRADICTED, which implied a product or kernel defect: focusing Review then arrow-keying left selection unmoved across two runs.
KEYBOARD_DIAGNOSIS_CORRECTED.correctedCause: PRE-HYDRATION READINESS, not the kernel. An independent audit isolated it: with networkidle plus a 4s settle, a real DOM click commits New and ArrowRight moves activeElement New -> Screen. The kernel and Segmented suites pass 25/25.
KEYBOARD_DIAGNOSIS_CORRECTED.whyIWasWrong: My probe measured a page that had rendered but not yet hydrated. Server-side markup was present and my readiness gate counts VISIBLE ELEMENTS, so it reported ready while no React handler was attached yet. A keyboard event against un-hydrated markup does nothing, which is indistinguishable from a broken kernel if you only look at the outcome.
KEYBOARD_DIAGNOSIS_CORRECTED.thisIsTheSameClassAgain: Fourth instance of an instrument returning a confident answer about a property it could not measure. Presence-not-paint, presence-not-geometry, surface-node-not-pseudo, and now rendered-not-hydrated. Every one of them made a green or a red that was not real.
KEYBOARD_DIAGNOSIS_CORRECTED.whatIsStillUNPROVEN: This is only PARTIAL validation and must not be read as keyboard credit. Entry to the control still used programmatic focus, so real Tab traversal and :focus-visible remain unproved. Arrow movement within an already-focused group is a weaker property than reaching that group by keyboard in the first place.
KEYBOARD_DIAGNOSIS_CORRECTED.requiredFix: capture-lab must fail closed on a DETERMINISTIC CLIENT-HYDRATION SENTINEL — visible SSR element counts and domcontentloaded are both insufficient. Only after that sentinel passes may it exercise page.keyboard Tab plus arrows and assert both selection change and :focus-visible.
KEYBOARD_DIAGNOSIS_CORRECTED.scoreEffect: interaction-states-motion stays at 3/5. The correction removes a false product defect but adds no evidence: nothing about real Tab or focus-visible is proven yet.
